slides.1.title: Climate Change — Harvest Date and Alcohol Level Analysis
slides.1.content:
This course systematically examines cross-region climate research for the Loire Valley, helping you build a solid knowledge framework. Key findings: since the 1980s, Loire harvest dates have advanced by an average of 2–3 weeks; average alcohol levels have increased by 1–1.5%; and the frequency of extreme vintages (frost, drought, heat) has risen significantly.

Through systematic study, you will be able to identify the typical styles of these AOCs and accurately describe their characteristics during tasting.
slides.2.title: Quiz
slides.2.questions.0.question: Which of the following best describes this course's research scope?
slides.2.questions.0.explanation: This course focuses on cross-region climate research for the Loire Valley, studying the impact of global warming on harvest timing, alcohol levels, acidity, and sweetness across all Loire sub-regions. Loire, as one of France's northernmost quality wine regions, is particularly sensitive to climate change — warming brings earlier ripeness but also frost risk, drought stress, and new challenges for producing traditional styles.
